title: Personal Credit Cards: Delinquency, Suspension and Charge-Off
content:
When minimum payments on Personal Credit Cards go unpaid, the account's days past due drive two escalations: suspension of the right to make charges, and charge-off of the balance.

## Days past due

The count runs in calendar days from the earliest due date whose minimum payment is still outstanding. It drops back to zero once every overdue minimum payment has been paid.

## Escalation

| Tier | Charging suspended on reaching this many days past due | Balance charged off on reaching this many days past due |
|---|---|---|
| Secured Visa | 60 | 180 |
| College Rewards Visa | 60 | 180 |
| Platinum Low Rate Visa | 60 | 180 |
| Cash Rewards Visa | 60 | 180 |
| Travel Rewards Visa Signature | 60 | 180 |
| Visa Infinite Private Client | 60 | 180 |

- Reaching the suspension level moves an active account to suspended, and no further charges can be made on it.
- A suspended account returns to active once its days past due are back at zero.
- Reaching the charge-off level charges off the balance, and every rewards point on the account is lost at that moment. The balance is still owed and goes to recovery, which lies outside this charter.
- A charged-off account is later closed by the bank as an administrative matter.

Repayment plans, settlements and hardship arrangements for overdue balances fall outside this page.

## Points of judgement (hypothetical)

- An account with one unpaid minimum from a due date 59 days ago is still active; on the following day it reaches 60 and is suspended.
- A suspended account whose cardholder pays every overdue minimum returns to zero days past due and so to active status, even if a balance not yet due remains.
